source: MAFF / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), Royal Government of Cambodia — ខ្សែសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំស្វាយចន្ទីនៅកម្ពុជា (Cashew Value Chain Study in Cambodia), field survey report (250 household respondents across major cashew-growing provinces), 2017, 57pp
text:
Comparison of tree loss/damage causes between local Khmer cashew variety and the improved M23 variety, from farmer-survey data in the 2017 MAFF cashew value chain study (n=250 households, multiple responses possible).

Reported causes of cashew tree loss or decline, Khmer variety vs. M23 variety (count / percent of respondents): natural disaster or drought - 7 (2.8%) vs. 4 (1.6%); pests and diseases - 82 (32.8%) vs. 110 (44%); termites - 12 (4.8%) vs. 14 (5.6%); lack of access to pesticide - 2 (0.8%) vs. 0; cause unknown/no answer - 9 (3.6%) vs. 1 (0.4%).

Pests and diseases were by far the leading cause of tree loss for both varieties, and notably more severe for the M23 variety (44% of respondents) than for the traditional local Khmer variety (32.8% of respondents).

At the individual-tree level, the report cites that about 44% of farmers growing M23 reported pest damage and about 7% reported disease on their M23 trees, compared to about 33% reporting pest damage and about 5% reporting disease on their local Khmer variety trees.

A notable farmer observation recorded in the report: in mixed orchards where both varieties are planted side by side, local Khmer variety trees were often unaffected while nearby M23 trees suffered damage — suggesting a genuine varietal difference in susceptibility rather than simply differing exposure to pests. This is a relevant consideration for farmers deciding whether to convert fully to M23 or maintain a mix of varieties.
caveat: Some specific figures in this source (percentages, price points, yield ranges) were transcribed from a scanned document at a resolution where certain digits were hard to confirm with full pixel-level certainty. Figures are reported as best-effort readings of the source; anyone using exact numbers for decisions should verify against the original report where possible.
